graph.title: LEGO 70127 Wolf Legend Beast
notes: Fixed the 4 separate groups. The booklet builds one model, the wolf, with the minifig riding on it. The minifig itself (head, torso, legs, headgear) is not in the parts list, so it has no nodes. The minifig's hand bar (b44) and shield (b45) are linked to the wolf's back plate (b5) by contact edges. The shield is linked to b44 for lack of a minifig node. The trading card (b42) is a loose item that ships with the set, so I linked it to b5 by a contact edge only to keep the graph connected.
The sword (b43) joins the hand bar (b44) by its bar holder.

The step pictures are small, so the exact stud-to-stud stacking is my best reading. Most ports are null. This applies mainly to the body plates on b5 (towball plates b7, b8, b11, b12; plates b6, b9, b13; wedge b14; bracket b16), the head stack (b19-b36), and the front-leg stack (f5-f9). Which part sits on which is a guess in those areas.
Legs hook onto towballs with socket plates: rear legs onto b11 and b12 at the tail end, front legs onto b7 and b8 at the head end. The head hooks onto b15. Which ball takes which leg is assumed.

The rear leg is built twice, with the second copy mirrored. The front leg is built twice and looks identical in both copies. The paw is built 4 times, and each paw's towball clicks into a leg's bottom socket plate.
The one sticker sheet (b41) is linked to the parts that take stickers: head cap b34, leg caps and tiles, and the paws. I put one sticker edge on b16 as a guess.
The 6141 round plates sit between the 4081b clip plates and the curved bricks. I modelled them as stud joints, not clip joints.
